figures.caption: Figure 1: Comparison of FER paradigms. Previous methods rely on passive reasoning over fixed inputs, while ActFER performs tool-augmented agentic inspection.

Figure 6: Qualitative comparison between ActFER with adaptive zoom and the same model without zoom on subtle expressions. Adaptive zoom reveals weak local cues and reduces confusion between similar expressions.
Figure 2: Overall architecture of ActFER. The agent combines tool-augmented visual reasoning, perceptual tools, FACS-grounded hierarchical inference, and two-stage SFT+UC-GRPO optimization.

Figure 7: Qualitative case study of ActFER on an anger example. The model first aligns the face, then invokes zoom_in on task-relevant regions, analyzes local AU evidence in a region-by-region manner, and finally synthesizes the observations into the final prediction. More qualitative examples are provided in the supplementary materials.
Figure 3: Statistics of the curated training data.
